title: The Farmer of Ur
description_from_course_sequence: A farmer receives a small payment of shekels from the temple after his work on the fields. At the city market, he must stretch this limited sum between barley — the staple grain his family depends on — and wool from the herders’ flocks, needed to prepare clothing for the coming winter.

title: The Peasant of Anyang
description_from_course_sequence: A peasant receives a small payment in cowrie shells after contributing labor to the fields. At market, it must be weighed - use these scarce shells on grain for winter storage or use them towards the repair of a communal stone sickle needed by several families for the harvest.

title: The Herder of Upper Niger
description_from_course_sequence: A herder receives ten rings of gold dust. With this limited wealth, the herder must decide whether to contribute millet to the village granary or purchase iron tools to repair the cattle pens.

title: The People of Olmec
description_from_course_sequence: The people of Olmec must choose whether to devote its labor to maize fields for survival or to acquiring obsidian blades for rituals believed to sustain the gods and preserve cosmic order.

title: The People of the Ancient Caribbean
description_from_course_sequence: The people of the Saladoid culture must decide whether to spend more labor on cultivating cassava for subsistence or on producing decorated ceramics used in trade and ritual exchange.

title: Hellenistic Greece + Maurya India
description_from_course_sequence: Merchants in Hellenistic Greece crave spices and textiles, while the courts of Maurya India prize silver and luxury goods.

title: Egypt + Rome
description_from_course_sequence: Cleopatra VII of Egypt is rich in grain and entangled with Rome; consider trade with a civilization rich in military power and wine.

title: Silk Road Sogdian: who will buy silk, and at what price?
description_from_course_sequence: A Sogdian Trader after the fall of Rome anticipates Roman elite vs Byzantine demand and willingness to pay.

title: Carolingian blacksmith: spearheads vs ox yokes
description_from_course_sequence: Decide whether to scale up spearheads or ox yokes as wars drive requisitions and disrupt farm labor.

title: Basra farmer Zayd: wheat tracking, algebra
description_from_course_sequence: Track wheat production and introduce algebraic methods for market problems.

title: Kilwa ivory merchant: competing buyers
description_from_course_sequence: Determine ivory quantities and price given Gujarati textile traders and Abbasid spice merchants.

title: Acre trader: crusader luxury demand
description_from_course_sequence: Luxury demand rises with crusaders and pilgrims; staple demand declines as sieges end.

title: Hangzhou tea: bumper harvest → levies
description_from_course_sequence: Supply shifts right (harvest) then left (transport levies).

title: Aztec cacao: festival demand ↑, poor harvest ↓ supply
description_from_course_sequence: Demand up among nobility while harvest failure reduces supply.

title: Florence cloth: plague shock
description_from_course_sequence: Weavers decimated (supply ↓) and luxury demand falls (demand ↓).

title: Bruges Flemish cloth (standardized, many sellers)
description_from_course_sequence: Horizontal demand at market price; standardized goods enable perfect substitution.

title: West African salt necessity
description_from_course_sequence: Essential good with no substitutes → vertical demand curve.

title: Banda nutmeg after Melaka tariff
description_from_course_sequence: Price increase → buyers reduce purchases sharply.

title: Florentine silk during war
description_from_course_sequence: Luxury demand highly elastic; raising price cuts Q sharply.

title: Gao salt: demand steady despite shocks
description_from_course_sequence: Caravan attacks reduce supply; demand remains steady (inelastic).

title: Taíno barter moves to 1:1
description_from_course_sequence: Trade ratios converge to 1‑to‑1, illustrating unit elasticity.

title: Venetian pepper after Portuguese route
description_from_course_sequence: Lower prices but total revenue falls → elastic demand.

title: Ming Suzhou rice: 10%↓P → 10%↑Qd
description_from_course_sequence: State granary releases induce ~unit‑elastic demand response.

title: Potosí mita labor demand
description_from_course_sequence: Forced mining labor demand remains high despite rising costs.

title: Dutch tulip panic
description_from_course_sequence: Small price increases collapse sales; TR plummets.

title: Istanbul coffee & sugar
description_from_course_sequence: Sugar price drop raises coffee demand (complements).

title: Great Frost constrains grain
description_from_course_sequence: Severe weather limits output despite high prices (inelastic supply).

title: Luanda textiles: Indian vs European cottons
description_from_course_sequence: Price up in one good shifts demand to the substitute.

title: Isfahan craftsman household: staples & modest luxuries ↑
description_from_course_sequence: Income growth → higher demand for normal goods.

title: Bengal weavers scale quickly
description_from_course_sequence: Higher bids → rapid output expansion (elastic supply).

title: Tokugawa peasant: millet ↓, polished rice ↑
description_from_course_sequence: Income rises → demand for inferior millet falls.

title: Kano caravan market rate
description_from_course_sequence: Haggling converges on a going rate; Qs = Qd by day’s end.

title: Canton tea under Qing monopoly (Canton System)
description_from_course_sequence: Guild licensing, information flows, and enforcement stabilize prices, limit competition.

title: Yunnan salt clearing price
description_from_course_sequence: Prices adjust until supply and demand align; market clears.

title: Boston tea after Tea Act
description_from_course_sequence: Lower prices expand consumer surplus (amid political boycott).

title: Calcutta cotton cloth flood
description_from_course_sequence: Lower prices increase consumer surplus; pressure on weavers.

title: Eden Treaty lowers tariffs
description_from_course_sequence: Lower trade barriers boost total surplus on both sides.

title: Saint‑Domingue sugar peak demand
description_from_course_sequence: Tight supply raises price well above unit cost; surplus accrues to planters.

title: Paris bread price cap
description_from_course_sequence: Ceiling keeps bread cheap but causes shortages.

title: Saint‑Domingue upheaval → sugar shortage
description_from_course_sequence: Output down, price up → both consumer & producer surplus shrink.

title: Philadelphia minimum wheat price
description_from_course_sequence: Floor supports farm income; warehouses fill with surplus.

title: Savannah cotton under industrial demand
description_from_course_sequence: Higher prices/assured offtake raise producer surplus.

title: Fiji copra under collusive low prices
description_from_course_sequence: Restrictive colonial practices shrink gains from trade (DWL).

title: Milk to Manhattan via rail depots
description_from_course_sequence: Wholesaler control, health inspection, and logistics determine price, quantity, margins.

title: English enclosure → rising rents
description_from_course_sequence: Commons enclosed; poor migrate; ownership concentrates.

econ_concept: Markets for the Factors of Production
title: Egyptian corvée for cotton canals
description_from_course_sequence: Land centralization, rising rents, and forced labor.

econ_concept: Markets for the Factors of Production
title: Javanese cultivation system quotas
description_from_course_sequence: State quotas divert labor from subsistence; revenues to Amsterdam.

econ_concept: Markets for the Factors of Production
title: Mexican hacienda peonage (land debt)
description_from_course_sequence: Wages in store credit, land concentration, coercive contracts.

econ_concept: Markets for the Factors of Production
title: US railroads: land grants, private capital, exploited labor
description_from_course_sequence: Public land supports private accumulation; immigrant/prison labor builds lines.

econ_concept: Markets for the Factors of Production
title: Brazilian coffee: slavery → indenture → wage
description_from_course_sequence: Transition in labor regimes; autonomy vs coercion.

title: Incheon textile mill under Japanese investors
description_from_course_sequence: Rural‑urban migration; colonial wage structures limit pay.

econ_concept: Markets for the Factors of Production
title: Ashanti cocoa smallholders & co‑ops
description_from_course_sequence: Smallholders pool capital, hire labor; export market shaped from below.

title: Sheffield munitions: women & migrants
description_from_course_sequence: War mobilization raises wages; reshapes roles & bargaining power.

title: Chicago credit freeze (Great Depression)
description_from_course_sequence: Bank collapses and soaring rates shrink investment and spending.

title: West German industry & Marshall Plan credit
description_from_course_sequence: Low‑interest financing enables rapid rebuilding and growth.

title: US mortgage refinance during GFC
description_from_course_sequence: Tightened lending and risk premiums raise borrowing costs/denials.
